sources.citation: Mira, Gustia; Elva Yusanti; Ilsa Dewita Putri Soraya; Rahmadina. 2021. Kamus Melayu Jambi Dialek Suku Anak Dalam-Indonesia. Jambi: Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Jambi. xvii+107 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Front matter (Petunjuk Pemakaian pp. xi-xii) notes only that /r/ is realised as [gh]; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: McDowell, Jonathan & Karl Anderbeck. 2020. The Malay Lects of Southern Sumatra. JSEALS Special Publication 7. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Includes a Kubu (Anak Dalam) site at Sungai Kijang (Rawas, South Sumatra) and sec. 5.12.4.3 'Kubu (Anak Dalam)'; only segmental/historical innovations (e.g. *r devoicing, -ko suffix). No statement on stress or accent anywhere in the volume.

sources.citation: Rozelin, Diana & Umar Fauzan. 2020. Education and Proto Language Maintenance at Orang Rimba in Jambi Province. IJELTAL 5(1): 177-193. doi:10.21093/ijeltal.v5i1.575
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Dialectometric/lexical and Proto-Malayic reflex study of Orang Rimba isolects; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Anderbeck, Karl Ronald. 2008. Malay Dialects of the Batanghari River Basin (Jambi, Sumatra). SIL e-Books 6. Dallas: SIL International. 173 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.2.1 p. 28 (Jambi Malay phoneme system): 'Stress regularly falls on the ultimate syllable.' fn.22: 'This is true in elicitation mode. Tadmor (p.c.) has suggested that JM accent might more correctly be described as utterance final.' This statement is for Jambi Malay (jamb1236) from the author's own 13 JM sites; Kubu is explicitly excluded from 'Jambi Malay' and treated separately in sec. 3.9 (pp. 54-56) only from secondary wordlists (Maryono et al. 1997), covering *h retention and penultimate schwa > o; Appendix E Kubu wordlists carry no stress marks. Nothing on Kubu stress.

sources.citation: Sager, Steven. 2008. The Sky is our Roof, the Earth our Floor: Orang Rimba Customs and Religion in the Bukit Duabelas Region of Jambi, Sumatra. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl:1885/49351
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'A Note on the Orthography' p. xvi: Rimba dialect 'very glottal', r often with glottal stop, initial h-/r- weak, final -s > -y; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hagen, Bernhard. 1908. Die Orang Kubu auf Sumatra. Frankfurt a. M.: Joseph Baer. (Veroeffentlichungen aus dem Staedtischen Voelker-Museum Frankfurt am Main 2.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 150-151 (chapter VII, Sprache): Kubu speak the local Malay dialect; Rawas-Kubu met by van Hasselt/Forbes spoke it 'mit einer fremden Betonung' / 'verdorbenes Malayisch mit besonderem Akzent' — impressionistic only, no placement rule. Anhang I Woerterliste (pp. 221-241) has no accent marking.

sources.citation: Rozelin, Diana. 2024. Kubu. In L. Körtvélyessy & P. Štekauer (eds.), Onomatopoeia in the World's Languages, ch. 72. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: The only grammar sketch of Kubu (Glottolog's top descriptive ref); Pusat Bahasa 'Struktur' volumes routinely contain a Fonologi chapter with a 'tekanan' (stress) subsection. Open PDF exists on the ministry EPrints server (record 26258) but the host is currently unreachable and not in the Internet Archive.
